mentions.name: Crit
mentions.description: This open source, local-first tool supports reviewing markdown and code output produced by AI agents. It adapts a GitHub PR-style review workflow to quick, local iterations, integrates into daily use with agents like Claude, is available via Homebrew core, and is gaining team-oriented sharing features designed for deployment inside private networks.
mentions.source_excerpt:
It's been three months now of building Crit - https://crit.md - local first, open source tool for reviewing markdown and code output from your favourite AI agent.

It's inspired by GitHub PR review workflow, only with quick iterations and local.

mentions.name: crit
mentions.description: A CLI tool for reviewing AI coding agent output like a GitHub PR. It lets users annotate and push back on AI-generated changes without creating a full pull request, and works on both agent plans and code itself.
mentions.problem: Claude Code and Cursor produce plausible-but-wrong changes with no easy way to annotate and push back on them without making a full PR.
mentions.source_excerpt:
https://crit.md - a CLI tool for reviewing AI coding agent output like a GitHub PR.

I got frustrated with Claude Code and Cursor producing plausible-but-wrong changes with no easy way to annotate and push back, without making a full PR. crit makes the review stage fun again!

Works on both plans as well as code itself.

mentions.name: crit
mentions.description: An MIT-licensed, open-source tool for reviewing plans and output from LLM agents. It offers a GitHub-style PR review experience for long markdown and diffs, which works better than terminal chat for reviewing agent work. It is offline-first and ships as a single binary.
mentions.problem: Terminal chat is a poor fit for reviewing long markdown plans and diffs produced by LLM agents; a PR-review-style interface works better.
mentions.audience: Engineers reviewing plans and output from LLM agents
mentions.source_excerpt: building crit to help reviewing plans & output from LLM agents - it has boosted my productivity a lot personally and I had a lot of nice feedback from other experienced engineers finding value in it - turns out while terminal is a nice way to chat with agents, GitHub-esque PR review wins for long markdown and diff view :)

evidence.value: building crit to help reviewing plans & output from LLM agents - it has boosted my productivity a lot personally and I had a lot of nice feedback from other experienced engineers finding value in it - turns out while terminal is a nice way to chat with agents, GitHub-esque PR review wins for long markdown and diff view :)
